    Consequences of retractions with nilpotent kernels #

    If a functor Ψ : 𝒞 ⥤ Mod A has retractions (Definition 2.4) and every composite of n maps in their kernels vanishes, then Ψ preserves indecomposability and reflects isomorphism classes (Section 1.4 and the end of the proof of Proposition 2.5). Indecomposability in 𝒞 means: the identity is nonzero and the only idempotent endomorphisms are 0 and 1.
